name: Agate Grey
lede: Agate Grey is a pale, neutral grey standardized by the RAL paint system, and in our archive it is overwhelmingly a highlight color.

sections.title: A stone's name on a paint chart
sections.body:
The library dates Agate Grey to RAL color 7038, with an approximate screen value, and to the ISCC-NBS block 264 of 1955 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary also carries the name, first recorded in 1789, more than a century before RAL existed [1]. Agate is a banded quartz, but our sources do not say whether this color was ever matched to the stone itself, so that link is undocumented here [1].

In LCH terms it measures lightness 74, chroma 5, hue 129 degrees, a color close enough to neutral that the nearest everyday name on file is [[ash]], about 3.7 units of ΔE away [1]. Among named greys it sits beside [[grey]], [[charcoal]] and [[taupe]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this grey in 1,595 of 23,781 paintings, 6.7 percent, among the more common matches we track, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match, a 1164 painting of the guardian figure Seitaka Dōji, long predates both the RAL and Maerz and Paul records, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It peaks in the 1940s, in 7 of 28 paintings, at 3.7 times the archive's overall rate, and Frederic Remington carries it in half of his 16 paintings here [2]. Inside a painting it overwhelmingly plays a highlight, in 92 percent of its appearances [2].

origin.named_after: the banded quartz agate, link to the stone undocumented

questions.q: Which paint system standardizes Agate Grey as color 7038?

openers: A pale grey that, in our archive, almost always plays the highlight, not the shadow.
